# Pink envelope in CSS

## Context
Ashley is redoing the portfolio as a letter. First step: recreate the pink vellum envelope from `envelope-pink.jpg` in pure CSS. The experience (what happens on load/click, where the portfolio content lives) comes later, so this is a standalone, reusable component and does not touch the current site.

## Reference (what the CSS must capture)
- Translucent pink vellum envelope, landscape, slight tilt (~ -4deg), soft shadow on a warm off-white ground.
- Open flap: triangular, folded back above the body, lighter pink, with a visible fold edge.
- Body: V-shaped side/bottom folds that read as overlapping translucent layers (darker pink where layers overlap, lighter where single).
- Cream card tucked inside, tilted (~ -12deg), poking out above the body. Card text shows faintly through the front panel (vellum effect).

## Approach
New files only (existing `index.html`, `css/style.css`, `css/_base.css` untouched):
- `envelope.html` - minimal page, loads `css/_base.css` + `css/envelope.css`.
- `css/envelope.css` - the component.

Structure: `.envelope > .envelope-back, .card, .envelope-front, .flap`.
- Size/colors driven by custom properties (`--env-w`, `--pink`, `--pink-deep`, `--card`) so it scales with one value.
- Triangles via `clip-path: polygon()` (not border hacks) for the flap and the left/right/bottom folds.
- Vellum: semi-transparent `rgba` pink layers with `mix-blend-mode: multiply` for overlap darkening, plus a subtle `backdrop-filter: blur()` on the front panel so the card text ghosts through.
- Depth: layered `box-shadow` / `filter: drop-shadow` on the whole envelope; soft gradient on the flap for the fold.
- Card: cream background, subtle paper grain via CSS gradient, placeholder script-style text (Google Font, e.g. a flourish script) just to check show-through. Real letter content comes later.
- Flap and card driven by `transform` with a `.is-open` class and a transition, so the later "experience" can open/close it. Default state = open, matching the image.
- Responsive: width `min(90vw, 560px)`, everything in `%`/`em` relative to the envelope.

## Verification
- Open `envelope.html` in a browser (local static server) and compare side by side with `envelope-pink.jpg` at desktop and ~400px widths; screenshot to check.
- Toggle `.is-open` in devtools to confirm the flap/card transition works.
- Confirm the existing `index.html` is unchanged (`git status` shows only the new files).

## Out of scope (waiting on Ashley's walkthrough)
Letter content, scroll/click interaction, replacing the current portfolio homepage.

- **Vellum look:** the body is semi-transparent pink, and the card's script text ghosts through the front panel like in your photo.

- **Vellum effect:** it's close but less milky than the photo. I can lighten it further or soften the folds if you want.
- **Card text:** the card's lower half is not as faded as in the photo.

The blue envelope is built as its own page, separate from the pink one. I rendered the portrait and landscape ratios in headless Chrome. I didn't re-render after the last tweak (hiding a hairline seam under the awning). I also didn't test the click-to-lift animation, the Tall and Square buttons, or phone width.

Open `envelope-blue-preview.html` in a browser. The files are:
- `envelope-blue-preview.html`: the preview page.
- `css/envelope-blue.css`: the blue envelope styles.

Nothing in the pink envelope files or the live site changed.

**Dimensions:** the preview has buttons to compare four proportions:
- **Portrait 0.81:** matches your photo.
- **Tall 2:3**
- **Square**
- **Landscape 7:5**

Everything is laid out in percentages of the envelope, so switching ratio only stretches the shape. The width comes from `--env-w` (80% of the screen, up to 520px).

**What's recreated:** a rounded back panel, a postcard sticking out behind, and a cream note ("Let's Go Somewhere.") tilted slightly. Over the note sit three overlapping vellum folds on the left, right and bottom, which read darker where they overlap. Clicking the envelope lifts the note and postcard.

**Placeholders:** the postcard is a CSS awning, sky and hills, not your photo. To use a real image, set `--photo: url(...)` in `envelope-blue.css`. The seal at the bottom of the note is a plain white oval, not your emblem.

**Differences from the photo:**
- My blue is slightly lighter and more saturated.
- The folds are a bit more see-through than in the photo.
- It isn't pixel-matched, just the same structure and feel.

For portfolio content, portrait gives the note the most room, since its card is tall enough for a letter. Landscape suits a short intro better. Tell me which proportion feels right, and I can adjust the pink one to match.

Both changes are in `envelope-blue-preview.html` and `css/envelope-blue.css`, and it renders correctly at the portrait ratio. I only checked it in one headless-Chrome screenshot, so the click-to-lift, the in-note scroll and phone width are untested.

- **Comments:** you had already commented out the controls and hint, so I commented out the leftover ratio-switcher script as well. It stays in the file in case you want it back. The pink preview had no preview-only elements left. Nothing in the live site changed.
- **Postcard:** it now shows `media/folio-etc-beach.jpg`. I removed the placeholder awning and hills.

I made a few other changes:
- **Scrolling:** the full text is longer than the note, so the note scrolls inside, with the scrollbar hidden. The vellum folds ignore the mouse, so scrolling and link clicks pass through them.
- **Starts lifted:** the envelope now starts with the note pulled up, so more text sits above the translucent bottom fold. The rest of the text shows through the fold, softly blurred. Remove `is-lifted` from the `<div class="envelope-blue is-lifted">` tag to start it tucked in.
- **Click handling:** the toggle was a `<button>`, which can't contain links, so I changed it to a plain `<div>`. Clicking a link no longer lifts or lowers the letter. This also means the envelope can't be toggled from the keyboard right now. I can add that once you've settled the interaction.

The blue envelope's photo and note text are what I'd carry into the real portfolio. Walk me through the experience whenever you're ready.

# Pink envelope in CSS

## Context
Ashley is redoing the portfolio as a letter. First step: recreate the pink vellum envelope from `envelope-pink.jpg` in pure CSS. The experience (what happens on load/click, where the portfolio content lives) comes later, so this is a standalone, reusable component and does not touch the current site.

## Reference (what the CSS must capture)
- Translucent pink vellum envelope, landscape, slight tilt (~ -4deg), soft shadow on a warm off-white ground.
- Open flap: triangular, folded back above the body, lighter pink, with a visible fold edge.
- Body: V-shaped side/bottom folds that read as overlapping translucent layers (darker pink where layers overlap, lighter where single).
- Cream card tucked inside, tilted (~ -12deg), poking out above the body. Card text shows faintly through the front panel (vellum effect).

## Approach
Preview first, existing files untouched. Nothing in `index.html`, `css/style.css`, or `css/_base.css` is edited until Ashley approves the preview:
- `envelope-preview.html` - separate standalone preview page, loads `css/_base.css` (read-only) + `css/envelope.css`.
- `css/envelope.css` - the component.
Only after Ashley signs off on the preview do we discuss moving it into `index.html`.

Structure: `.envelope > .envelope-back, .card, .envelope-front, .flap`.
- Size/colors driven by custom properties (`--env-w`, `--pink`, `--pink-deep`, `--card`) so it scales with one value.
- Triangles via `clip-path: polygon()` (not border hacks) for the flap and the left/right/bottom folds.
- Vellum: semi-transparent `rgba` pink layers with `mix-blend-mode: multiply` for overlap darkening, plus a subtle `backdrop-filter: blur()` on the front panel so the card text ghosts through.
- Depth: layered `box-shadow` / `filter: drop-shadow` on the whole envelope; soft gradient on the flap for the fold.
- Card: cream background, subtle paper grain via CSS gradient, placeholder script-style text (Google Font, e.g. a flourish script) just to check show-through. Real letter content comes later.
- Flap and card driven by `transform` with a `.is-open` class and a transition, so the later "experience" can open/close it. Default state = open, matching the image.
- Responsive: width `min(90vw, 560px)`, everything in `%`/`em` relative to the envelope.

## Verification
- Open `envelope-preview.html` in a browser (local static server) and compare side by side with `envelope-pink.jpg` at desktop and ~400px widths; screenshot to check.
- Toggle `.is-open` in devtools to confirm the flap/card transition works.
- Confirm the existing `index.html` is unchanged (`git status` shows only the new files).

## Out of scope (waiting on Ashley's walkthrough)
Letter content, scroll/click interaction, replacing the current portfolio homepage.

## Current task: fit blue envelope to laptop viewport height
Problem (Ashley: "laptop, too tall"): width is capped at `min(80vw, 520px)`, but the envelope is portrait (H = W/0.81 ~ 640px) and the postcard sticks out above (~-11.5% top, ~-19% when lifted), plus 14vmin body padding-top. On a short laptop window the stack overflows the viewport height.

Fix (blue only; pink is landscape ~350px tall, not affected):
1. `css/envelope-blue.css`, `.envelope-blue`: make width height-aware:
   `--env-w: min(80vw, 520px, calc((100svh - 6vmin) * var(--ratio) / 1.22));`
   (1.22 = envelope height + ~19% postcard overhang + ~3% shadow). Keeps `--ratio` as the single proportion knob.
2. Same rule: `margin-top: calc(var(--env-w) / var(--ratio) * .2);` so the overhang is reserved inside the budget instead of relying on body padding.
3. `envelope-blue-preview.html` preview `body`: replace `padding: 14vmin 1rem 5vmin` with `padding: 3vmin 1rem`, and `min-height: 100vh` -> `100svh`.
4. Result: the whole stack (postcard to bottom edge) fits any window height, shrinking the envelope on short screens; width is unaffected on tall screens (still max 520px).

Verification: headless Chrome screenshots at 1440x700, 1280x800, 1440x900, and 390x844 (phone); confirm postcard top and envelope bottom are both inside the viewport with margin, with and without `.is-lifted`. Confirm text still readable (min 12px) and `git status` shows only the two blue files changed.

# Portfolio-as-a-letter: envelope components (status)

## Context
Ashley is redoing the portfolio as a letter. Envelopes are built as standalone previews, so the live site is untouched until they approve moving anything in. The interaction/experience is still to be walked through by Ashley.

## Done (all standalone, nothing in index.html/style.css/_base.css edited)
- Pink vellum envelope: `envelope-preview.html` + `css/envelope.css` (open flap, tilted card, `.is-open` toggle).
- Blue portrait envelope: `envelope-blue-preview.html` + `css/envelope-blue.css`.
  - Postcard = `media/folio-etc-beach.jpg`.
  - Cream note holds the About text, Work Sans (switched back from Instrument Serif; size 2.7cqw, min 12px, line-height 1.4). Note scrolls internally; folds are `pointer-events: none`.
  - Starts `.is-lifted`; click toggles (ignores link clicks). Ratio controls/hint/script commented out; portrait 0.81 only.

## Current task: fit blue envelope to laptop viewport height
Problem (Ashley: "laptop, too tall"): width is capped at `min(80vw, 520px)`, but the envelope is portrait (H = W/0.81 ~ 640px) and the postcard sticks out above (~-11.5% top, ~-19% when lifted), plus 14vmin body padding-top. On a short laptop window the stack overflows the viewport height.

Fix (blue only; pink is landscape ~350px tall, not affected):
1. `css/envelope-blue.css`, `.envelope-blue`: make width height-aware:
   `--env-w: min(80vw, 520px, calc((100svh - 6vmin) * var(--ratio) / 1.22));`
   (1.22 = envelope height + ~19% postcard overhang + ~3% shadow). Keeps `--ratio` as the single proportion knob.
2. Same rule: `margin-top: calc(var(--env-w) / var(--ratio) * .2);` so the overhang is reserved inside the budget instead of relying on body padding.
3. `envelope-blue-preview.html` preview `body`: replace `padding: 14vmin 1rem 5vmin` with `padding: 3vmin 1rem`, and `min-height: 100vh` -> `100svh`.
4. Result: the whole stack (postcard to bottom edge) fits any window height, shrinking the envelope on short screens; width is unaffected on tall screens (still max 520px).

Verification: headless Chrome screenshots at 1440x700, 1280x800, 1440x900, and 390x844 (phone); confirm postcard top and envelope bottom are both inside the viewport with margin, with and without `.is-lifted`. Confirm text still readable (min 12px) and `git status` shows only the two blue files changed.

## Open / next (waiting on Ashley)
- Walkthrough of the intended experience (what happens on load/click, where the other portfolio sections live).
- Whether to move the chosen envelope into `index.html`, and which one (pink or blue).
- Possible follow-ups: keyboard access for the toggle, tidy duplicate `.eb-note` rule in `envelope-blue.css`, mobile check.

  - Postcard = `media/folio-etc-beach.jpg`.

Problem (Ashley: "laptop, too tall"): width is capped at `min(80vw, 520px)`, but the envelope is portrait (H = W/0.81 ~ 640px) and the postcard sticks out above (~-11.5% top, ~-19% when lifted), plus 14vmin body padding-top. On a short laptop window the stack overflows the viewport height.

Fix (blue only; pink is landscape ~350px tall, not affected):
1. `css/envelope-blue.css`, `.envelope-blue`: make width height-aware:

message.content: does cutive mono have an italic version?

content.text:
No, Cutive Mono has only one style: Regular, weight 400. Google Fonts offers no italic or bold for it. If you set `font-style: italic` or `font-weight: bold`, the browser fakes it, slanting the regular letters or smearing them heavier. That looks cruder than a true italic.

That's why I set the letterhead name to `font-style: normal` earlier, so it never showed a faked slant. The letter doesn't currently use bold or italic anywhere.

If you want true italics or bold in the letter, these are close alternatives that have them:
- **Courier Prime:** has Regular, Italic, Bold and Bold Italic. It has a typewriter feel, but it's sturdier and a bit darker than Cutive Mono.
- **IBM Plex Mono:** has italic and a wider range of weights. It's cleaner and less like a typewriter.
- **Special Elite:** a distressed, worn-typewriter look. It has no italic either.

If you want to keep Cutive Mono, I'd keep emphasis out of the letter, or do it with spacing, caps or a second font such as the Pinyon Script you already use for the signature. Want me to try Courier Prime to compare?

**The header move** works, but it's half-finished, which is why the screenshot shows the letterhead overlapping the first paragraph. `div.letter-body` is positioned to fill the whole letter (`position: absolute; inset: 0`). The header is now a normal element in `div.letter`, so the body sits on top of it at the same spot. Four things were relying on the old position inside the body: - **Spacing:** the top padding (`12cqw 9cqw`) that gives the letterhead its margins came from `letter-body`. - **Text size:** `letter-body` sets the font size (15px) and line-height. Outside it, the header text falls back to the page's larger default, and the letterhead title and date come out too big. - **Paragraph margins:** your global `p { margin: 40px 0 }` was being cancelled by `div.letter-body p { margin: 0 }`. Outside the body, the header's `

`s get the 40px margins back. - **Scrolling:** inside the body, the letterhead scrolls away with the text. Outside it, it stays put. I haven't changed anything. To make it work, I need to know how the header should behave: 1. **Pinned:** the letterhead stays at the top of the letter and the body text scrolls underneath. This is the usual reason to move it out. It costs about 3–4 lines of readable space, which matters since the visible part of the letter above the fold is small. 2. **Scrolls with the text:** it looks like it did before, so there's no point in moving it out. If you want it pinned, I'd make `div.letter` a column (header on top, body filling the rest), move the padding and font settings onto the header, and shrink the body's top padding. Should I do that? **`div.envelope-back`** is the envelope's back panel. It's the first child of the envelope, a full-size rounded rectangle behind everything else. It has a gradient from `--tint-light` at the top to `--tint` below, with rounded top corners. It's what you see as the envelope's solid color where the postcard and letter don't cover it and the translucent folds aren't over it: around the top-right of the letter and as a strip along the letter's right edge. It also gives the folds a colored base to sit on, so their translucent layers read as vellum on paper. Without it, the folds would sit directly on the white page and the envelope would look hollow.
